title: Zesty Grassy Mexican Rice Pozole
description: A fluffy, cozy pozole packed with smoky ancho, fresh herbs, and a surprising grape nut cereal crunch, all cooked on a comal for a nut‑free, plant‑friendly twist.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a comal over medium heat and sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 4 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and crushed ancho chili pepper, cooking for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Stir in the soaked hominy kernels and reduce the heat to low, simmering uncovered for 30 minutes until the hominy is tender and the broth has thickened slightly.
During the last 5 minutes of simmering, season the pozole with cumin, salt, and lime juice, tasting to adjust flavor.
When the hominy is cooked, remove the pot from heat and stir in the chopped cilantro and parsley mix.
Transfer the pozole to a serving dish, spooning a generous portion of the fluffy rice into the center.
Sprinkle the grape nut cereal over the top for a crunchy, nut‑free finish.
Serve hot, optionally accompanied by sliced radishes, diced avocado, and extra lime wedges on the side.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
